title: Carlsen's endgame grind
summary: Chennai, 2013: in the world championship match, Carlsen presses an equal endgame for hours until Anand cracks.

steps.title: Chennai, 2013
steps.text: In 2013 Magnus Carlsen, aged twenty-two, challenged the world champion Viswanathan Anand in Chennai, in Anand's home country, India. The first four games were drawn. In game five Carlsen took a quiet, almost equal endgame and kept pressing. He won the game and later the match, becoming world champion.
steps.narration: Chennai, 2013. Magnus Carlsen challenges the world champion Viswanathan Anand. Game five: an equal endgame, and Carlsen will not let it go.

steps.title: Carlsen – Anand, World Championship, game 5, 2013
steps.text: The queens come off early and the position is close to equal. Most players would agree a draw. Carlsen keeps asking small questions, and late in the game Anand finally makes a slip.
steps.narration: An equal endgame, and a very patient Carlsen. Watch for the moment Anand slips, then find the winning plan.

notes.text: 15.Qxd8+: the queens come off early. Carlsen is happy to play an endgame.
29.e4: the position is almost level, but Carlsen keeps improving his pieces.
40.Rxg5: Carlsen grabs a pawn; Anand hits back on b3.
50...Rxg2: Anand wins a pawn back. It looks like a draw.
51...Ke6?: a natural move, but it is the mistake. Moving the rook to e2 at once was the better defence.
52.a4!: Carlsen lets the e-pawn go. The passed a-pawn is what counts.
58.h4: the a-pawn is about to promote and Black's rook is tied up. Anand resigned.

guesses.prompt: Find a check that leads to trading the bishops.
guesses.hint: Your bishop can check from g8, and later attack b3.
guesses.why: 47.Bg8+ drives the king back, and soon Bxb3 trades the bishops. Rook endgames are where Carlsen squeezes best.

guesses.prompt: Black's king just took the e5 pawn. What matters now?
guesses.hint: Your a-pawn is passed and far from Black's king. Run!
guesses.why: 53.a5: the a-pawn is far away from Black's king, and every step it takes is a new problem for Black.

guesses.prompt: The pawn is on a5. Black's king wants to run to the queenside. Stop it.
guesses.hint: Your rook can cut the king off along a rank.
guesses.why: 54.Rh7 cuts the black king off along the seventh rank, so it cannot reach the a-pawn in time.

guesses.prompt: The king is cut off. What now?
guesses.why: 55.a6: the pawn runs to a6 and then a7. Black's rook will have to sit in front of it.

steps.title: Endgame patience
steps.question: The endgame was almost equal for a long time. What did Carlsen do?

options.text: Kept making small, safe improvements until Anand made a mistake
options.why: Yes. Carlsen took no risks; he just kept asking questions, and one wrong answer was enough.
He kept playing for nearly sixty moves. That is the whole point of the game.

options.text: Sacrificed material to attack the king
options.why: There was no attack. The game was won by a passed pawn in a rook endgame.

steps.narration: The position was equal for hours. What was Carlsen's secret?

steps.title: Outside passed pawn
steps.text: In rook endgames, a passed pawn far from the enemy king is a huge asset. Carlsen gave up his e-pawn to free the a-pawn, cut Black's king off with his rook, and pushed. Just as important: he kept playing an equal position, because endgames reward the player who keeps asking questions.
steps.narration: Do not agree to a draw just because it is equal. Keep pressing, and when the chance comes, push the passed pawn.
